schemaNote: Shiplo Showcase #11 planet data. Mean values from NASA Planetary Fact Sheet; dayHours = sidereal rotation period; moons confirmed as of 2025 (counts still growing). Distances in astronomical units (AU). No runtime API: this file is the whole content source.
sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values), moon counts as of 2025.

planets.name: Mercury
facts: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days — the shortest in the Solar System.
With almost no atmosphere to hold heat, its nights turn bitterly cold.
Its cratered surface looks much like our Moon.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); sidereal rotation 58.6 Earth days.

planets.name: Venus
facts: Venus spins so slowly that one day there lasts 243 Earth days.
Thick sulfuric-acid clouds trap heat — Venus is hotter than Mercury.
It spins backwards: on Venus, the Sun rises in the west.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); sidereal rotation 243 Earth days, retrograde.

planets.name: Earth
facts: Earth is the only known world with liquid-water oceans on its surface.
One large Moon steadies Earth's tilt — and our seasons.
The planet's blue color, seen from space, is ocean and sky.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); the atlas's reference for day and year.

planets.name: Mars
facts: Rusty iron oxide in the soil gives Mars its red color.
It hosts Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System.
Dried riverbeds show water once flowed across Mars.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); moons: Phobos and Deimos.

planets.name: Jupiter
facts: Jupiter is the giant of the system — every other planet would fit inside.
Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth, raging for centuries.
For all its size, Jupiter has the shortest day: 9.9 hours.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); 95 confirmed moons as of 2025.

planets.name: Saturn
facts: Saturn's rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock.
The planet is so light it would float in a giant bathtub.
Saturn leads the moon count — well over two hundred confirmed.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); 274 confirmed moons as of 2025.

planets.name: Uranus
facts: Uranus rolls around the Sun on its side, tilted almost 98 degrees.
Methane high in its atmosphere paints the planet teal.
Each pole gets 42 years of sunlight, then 42 years of night.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); rotation retrograde, tilted axis ~98°.

planets.name: Neptune
facts: Neptune's winds are the fastest known — over 2,000 km/h.
Mathematicians found it before telescopes: its gravity gave it away.
One Neptune year lasts 165 Earth years — one orbit since its discovery.
planets.sourceNote: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (mean values); sidereal rotation 16.1 hours.
